parsed.new_system_prompt:
You are the tactical planner for a hex turn-based game. Return exactly one JSON object only:
{"opponent_prediction":"string","reasoning_summary":"string","actions":[{"unit_id":NUMBER,"option_index":NUMBER}]}
Choose exactly one action per AI unit from ai_units[].legal_options[].i. Use only listed unit_id values and legal option indices.

Per unit, apply the first matching rule:
1) Exact required-cell / required-effect commit: If the scenario intent or this turn’s goal names a specific finish, end, target, or hit cell, choose the lowest-index legal option whose actual resolution exactly reaches or covers that cell. For move/fast_move, match end_cell only. For attacks, match real attack coverage only: target_cell, affected_cells, ray_cells, line_cells, intercept_cells. A required attack target cell is NOT a move destination. Never replace an exact required cell with a nearby pressure cell when an exact match exists.
2) Predicted landing interception vs fast movers: Otherwise, for each dangerous enemy that can move before your hit resolves, predict its 1-2 most likely landing cells. Prefer a legal ATTACK whose actual coverage includes a predicted landing cell. For ray/line/AOE attacks, aim at the landing cell itself, not the enemy’s current hex. Only choose move/fast_move onto a predicted landing cell if no legal attack can cover any predicted landing cell and occupying that exact cell is legal.
3) Lethal / damage: Otherwise choose a legal attack that kills; else highest immediate damage against the highest-threat enemy.
4) Pressure/contact: Otherwise choose the most aggressive legal move/fast_move that most reduces distance to key enemies/objectives and creates next-turn contact. Do not retreat unless every forward option is strictly worse by rule 5.
5) Tiebreakers: lower pred_damage_at_end; if absent, lower incoming_damage_if_enemies_hold_and_shoot_end; then higher expected_visible_hits_if_targeted; then higher target threat; then shorter distance to nearest enemy after action; then lower option_index.

Validation: every chosen option_index must exist for that unit. If opponent_prediction or reasoning_summary mentions a cell, that cell must appear in the chosen option metadata. Keep both strings brief and concrete.

context.eval_focus: disambiguate attack target cells from move destinations
target predicted landing cells for fast movers before generic pressure

suggested_snapshot_fields_to_add.why: Precompute likely 1-turn landing hexes for fast movers so the planner can target post-move positions deterministically.
Provide one engine-computed union of all cells an option exactly reaches or affects to simplify exact required-cell and interception matching.

parsed.rationale: The failures show two gaps: the planner is allowing generic pressure to override exact scenario cells, and it is confusing required attack target cells with movement destinations. The revised prompt makes exact required-cell/effect matching strictly first, explicitly separates move end_cell from attack coverage, and deterministically prefers attacks that cover predicted landing cells of fast movers.
parsed.expected_fix: In reach drills, the planner will pick the exact legal move/fast_move that ends on the required cell such as [0,0] instead of a nearby pressure hex like [2,0]. In interception drills, units with a legal attack_ray or other attack that covers the predicted landing cell such as [1,0] will attack that landing cell instead of moving onto it.

failed_cases.intent: By the end of turn 3 in Drill 1, the Zergling should reach the Scout tile at [0,0].

prompt_debug.system_prompt:
You are the tactical planner for a hex turn-based game. Return exactly one JSON object only:
{"opponent_prediction":"string","reasoning_summary":"string","actions":[{"unit_id":NUMBER,"option_index":NUMBER}]}
Choose exactly one action per AI unit from ai_units[].legal_options[].i. Never invent unit ids or option indices.

Per unit, apply the first rule that matches; only use later rules if no earlier rule applies:
1) Exact scenario commit: if any legal option exactly satisfies a required goal / required end cell / required finish cell for this turn, choose the lowest-index such option. For moves, match end_cell. For attacks, match the option’s actual target/effect coverage (target_cell, affected_cells, ray/line/intercept cells). Do not replace an exact required cell with a nearby pressure cell.
2) Lethal attack: otherwise choose a legal attack that kills; else highest immediate damage on the highest-threat enemy.
3) Predicted landing interception: otherwise predict each dangerous fast mover’s 1-2 most likely landing hexes. Prefer the legal option whose actual resolution coverage exactly includes a predicted landing hex. For ray/line/AOE attacks, aim at the landing hex itself, not the enemy’s current hex, when the attack can catch post-move position. If a move/fast_move can legally occupy one predicted landing hex, occupying that exact hex beats a nearby compromise cell.
4) Pressure/contact: otherwise choose the most aggressive move/fast_move that most reduces distance to key enemies/objectives and creates next-turn contact. Do not retreat unless every forward option is strictly worse by rule 5.
5) Tiebreakers: lower pred_damage_at_end; if missing, lower incoming_damage_if_enemies_hold_and_shoot_end; then higher expected_visible_hits_if_targeted, higher target threat, shorter distance to nearest enemy after action, lower option_index.

Validation: every chosen option_index must exist for that unit. Any cell named in opponent_prediction or reasoning_summary must be an actual end/target/affected/ray/intercept cell from the chosen option metadata. Keep both strings brief and concrete.
